identity.name: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
alt_names: German Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia

land.text: 'the remaining Czech parts of Czechoslovakia' that German troops entered on the morning of 15 March 1939

predecessors.note: The Second Czechoslovak Republic; Cliopatria's Czechoslovakia row has no shape for 1939-1946.

land.text: the Czech lands; the infobox names the Third Czechoslovak Republic as successor

successors.note: The Sudetenland, which the Reich held from October 1938, returned to the Third Czechoslovak Republic separately (the czechoslovakia and nazi-germany dossiers).

rulers.name: Emil Hácha
rulers.title: State President
rulers.note: Infobox 'Head of state 1939–1945: Emil Hácha' (president since November 1938). The real power was the Reichsprotektor: Konstantin von Neurath 21 March 1939 - 24 August 1943 (Reinhard Heydrich acting 29 September 1941 - 4 June 1942, Kurt Daluege acting 5 June 1942 - 24 August 1943), then Wilhelm Frick 24 August 1943 - 8 May 1945.

correction.text: Bohemia and Moravia without the Sudetenland, which 'the German Reich had annexed ... in October 1938' (Czechoslovakia's 1938 shape inside Czechia)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no shape for the Czech lands in 1939-1945 (its Czechoslovakia row jumps from 1938 to 1947). The pages give no area (the infobox has only 'about 7,380,000 inhabitants in 1940'), so the area check is: page silent. The spec resolves to about 38,000 km2. The page names the Sudetenland as excluded (annexed by the Reich in October 1938) and does not mention Hlučín or Zaolzie; Zaolzie 'became part of Nazi Germany after the German invasion of Poland in September 1939' (occupation page), so it is outside this shape. Whether Czechoslovakia's 1938 shape in Czechia already omits Hlučín is not checked.

region.text: Bohemia and Moravia without the Sudetenland, which 'the German Reich had annexed ... in October 1938' (Czechoslovakia's 1938 shape inside Czechia)

ledger.note: 16 March 1939: Hitler proclaims the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia from Prague Castle. 'Adolf Hitler established the protectorate on 16 March 1939, issuing a proclamation from Prague Castle'; German troops had entered the Czech lands on the morning of 15 March (German occupation of Czechoslovakia page). Infobox status: 'nominal Protectorate and partially annexed territory within Nazi Germany'.

region.text: Bohemia and Moravia without the Sudetenland, which 'the German Reich had annexed ... in October 1938' (Czechoslovakia's 1938 shape inside Czechia)

ledger.note: 15 March 1939: German troops occupy the Czech lands. 'On the morning of 15 March, German troops entered the remaining Czech parts of Czechoslovakia'; the czechoslovakia dossier records the same occupation from the owner's side.

region.text: Bohemia and Moravia without the Sudetenland, which 'the German Reich had annexed ... in October 1938' (Czechoslovakia's 1938 shape inside Czechia)

ledger.note: 8-9 May 1945: German rule ends in the Czech lands. 'On 5 May, a national uprising began spontaneously in Prague'; 'On 8 May, the German Wehrmacht capitulated'; 'Prague was taken on 9 May by Soviet troops during the Prague Offensive'.

region.text: the Protectorate, which the infobox says was succeeded by the Third Czechoslovak Republic

ledger.note: May 1945: the Protectorate ends. 'The state's existence came to an end with the surrender of Germany to the Allies in May 1945'; the infobox names the Third Czechoslovak Republic as successor. The page gives no day for the liberation of Prague.

wars.name: Prague uprising

zones.text: Prague, where 'a national uprising began spontaneously' on 5 May 1945

wars.outcome: The Czech uprising began 5 May 1945; the Wehrmacht capitulated 8 May and Soviet troops took Prague on 9 May during the Prague offensive, ending the Protectorate.
wars.note: The Prague uprising and Prague offensive articles themselves were not opened (page budget); the dates come from the German occupation page.

certainty.note: The border with the Reich follows the October 1938 Sudetenland line, itself set by the Munich Agreement; the Protectorate's land boundary did not change in six years.

sources.title: Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia
sources.note: Identity, 16 March 1939 proclamation, capital, Hácha, Reichsprotektors, 7,380,000 inhabitants in 1940, end May 1945. The page has no area figure, no Hlučín/Těšín and no liberation date.

sources.title: German occupation of Czechoslovakia
sources.note: 15 March 1939 entry of German troops, Zaolzie to Germany September 1939, Prague uprising 5 May, German capitulation 8 May and Soviet entry 9 May 1945.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the Czech lands for 1939-1946. The relation to Germany is recorded as occupation_start/end (the owner's side of the czechoslovak dossier's event) because the infobox calls it a 'nominal Protectorate and partially annexed territory'; the nazi-germany dossier records the same land under czechoslovakia. The infobox has no area; the 'about 38,000 km2' of the resolved shape is a gazetteer figure, not a page figure (page silent). Party planning to divide the land between four Gaue ('Reichsgau Sudetenland, Gau Bayreuth, Reichsgau Niederdonau, Reichsgau Oberdonau') was never carried out; 'Hitler stated as late as 1943 that the issue was still to be decided'; no territorial change inside the Protectorate is recorded. Minister presidents (Beran 16 March - 27 April 1939, Eliáš to 2 October 1941, Krejčí 19 January 1942 - 19 January 1945, Bienert to May 1945) are in the page but not in the ruler strip. Hlučín (Hultschin) and Těšín (Zaolzie): the pages are silent on whether any part was inside the Protectorate.
